$comment: Every non-ASCII character the editor DRAWS WITH, and whether the declared UI font stack can render it. See scripts/check-glyph-coverage.mjs for why this is declared rather than measured, and decisions/131 for the capture that forced it. ADR-137 then removed the whole class: the editor no longer draws CONTROLS with characters at all — `theme/icons.tsx` does, on one grid at one stroke weight — so the sixty-nine characters that used to be icons are `forbidden` here, each naming the icon that replaced it. What is left `allowed` is typography: arrows and a minus sign inside prose, comparison operators inside rule text, and one box-drawing rule in an ASCII table.
fontStack: Inter, Segoe UI, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

U+23EE.name: BLACK LEFT-POINTING DOUBLE TRIANGLE WITH VERTICAL BAR
U+23EE.reason: a Unicode 6.0 (2010) Miscellaneous Technical media control. NOT ONE font in --mtk-font-ui (Inter / Segoe UI / system-ui / -apple-system / Helvetica Neue / Arial) contains it, so the browser leaves the declared stack entirely: .notdef on Linux, a colour Segoe UI Emoji glyph on Windows. Proven by progress/glyph-coverage/before/animation-timeline-tracks.png, where three of four transport buttons are empty boxes and the one that renders is U+25B6. Use <TransportIcon>.
